scope.flow: HypoVault performance-fee accounting via transferable shares and userBasis merging
scope.environment: HypoVault contract with Average Cost Basis accounting and ERC20 transferable shares

statements.text: Alice holds a highly profitable position where market value exceeds her cost basis.
Bob holds a position at a loss with a high-cost basis.
Bob transfers his shares to Alice, triggering _transferBasis.
The transferred proportional basis is added to Alice's existing userBasis, merging the losing high-cost basis into her low-cost basis.
_transferBasis adds incoming basis to the recipient's existing basis without distinguishing a pre-existing profitable position from the incoming position's financial history.
The merged average cost basis in Alice's account becomes artificially inflated to equal or exceed the current market value of the shares.
Calculated profit upon withdrawal becomes zero or negative, completely eliminating the performance fee.
Any two or more colluding users can systematically and completely evade performance fees, reducing protocol fee income to near zero if widely adopted.
A secondary market for selling high-cost losing basis to profitable users is created.

Performance fees should be charged on profitable withdrawals based on each position's own cost basis, so transferring shares must not allow a recipient's profit to be offset by an incoming loss position's basis.
Alice and Bob collude to execute the share transfer and withdrawal strategy.

ambiguities: Report does not specify exact numeric values for market value, basis, or fee amounts.
Report does not state whether the withdrawal step is a separate action or part of the same flow.
Fundamental unfairness and flawed economic model effects omitted as they are not directly observable outcomes.
Report does not establish that transfers are permissionless or that any unauthorized party can trigger them.
